title: Adic coefficient datum and reduction tower
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and use its small pro-etale site, constant coefficient sheaves, and derived categories of sheaves of modules [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq\Lambda$ be a finitely generated ideal, and put $P_n=\Lambda/I^n$ for integers $n\geq1$, with powers and quotient rings as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume $\Lambda/I$ is torsion as an additive group (each element is killed by a positive integer), and every $P_n$, placed in degree zero, is perfect over $\Lambda$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ define its reduction by derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]:
$$K_n:=K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}(P_n)_X\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},P_n).$$
Here $(P_n)_X$ and $\Lambda_X$ are constant sheaves of rings, and the underlying $\Lambda_X$-object is the derived tensor of [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Regard all reductions also in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ by restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For $b\geq a\geq1$, define $q_{b,a}:K_b\to K_a$ there using the quotient map $P_b\to P_a$. The transition identities are $q_{a,a}=1$ and $q_{c,a}=q_{b,a}\circ q_{c,b}$ for $c\geq b\geq a$. The canonical normalization isomorphisms are
$$\theta_{b,a}:K_b\otimes^L_{(P_b)_X}(P_a)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a.$$
They are the scalar-extension associativity maps. For $c\geq b\geq a$, the composite of $\theta_{c,b}\otimes^L_{(P_b)_X}(P_a)_X$ with $\theta_{b,a}$ equals $\theta_{c,a}$ after the canonical associativity identification of the source; for $b=a$ normalization is the unit identification.

proof.text: Choose one K-flat resolution $Q\to K$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], on the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the complex $Q_n=Q\otimes_{\Lambda_X}(P_n)_X$ is a model of $K_n$ in the derived category of $(P_n)_X$-modules, with canonical comparisons for different resolutions. Use these models to specify the tower and normalization maps. No boundedness of $K$ or flatness of $P_n$ over $\Lambda$ is required.

For $b\geq a$, $I^b\subseteq I^a$: write $I^b=I^aI^{b-a}$ and use that an ideal absorbs multiplication [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Thus $\pi_{b,a}:P_b\to P_a$ sends the class of $x$ to its class modulo $I^a$. On classes, $\pi_{a,a}=1$ and $\pi_{c,a}=\pi_{b,a}\circ\pi_{c,b}$. Define the chain map $Q_b\to Q_a$ by $u\otimes t\mapsto u\otimes\pi_{b,a}(t)$ using sheaf change of rings [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], then take its derived class after restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Restriction retains the underlying abelian sheaves and differentials, hence the same kernels, images and cohomology; it preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The two chain-map identities hold on the displayed generators in every degree and pass to the localization. For a chain map $h:Q\to Q'$, the comparison maps $h\otimes1$ commute with these transitions: both composites send $u\otimes t$ to $h(u)\otimes\pi_{b,a}(t)$. This equality also holds after inverting quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat models, so the canonical resolution comparisons of step 1 preserve the tower.

By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $Q_b$ is K-flat with flat terms over $(P_b)_X$. Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to $(P_b)_X\to(P_a)_X$: the source of $\theta_{b,a}$ is represented by $(Q\otimes_{\Lambda_X}(P_b)_X)\otimes_{(P_b)_X}(P_a)_X$. In each degree the map $(u\otimes t)\otimes s\mapsto u\otimes\pi_{b,a}(t)s$ has inverse $u\otimes s\mapsto(u\otimes1)\otimes s$. The balancing relations over both rings prove well-definedness, and their composites are identity by the relation $(u\otimes t)\otimes s=(u\otimes1)\otimes\pi_{b,a}(t)s$. These are maps of the sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]: the formulas commute with restriction and extend uniquely by sheafification. They commute with the differentials, which act on $u$, and are $(P_a)_X$-linear. Their derived classes give $\theta_{b,a}$, naturally and independently of the resolution by the canonical comparisons in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]: for a chain map $h:Q\to Q'$, either order of comparison and normalization sends $(u\otimes t)\otimes s$ to $h(u)\otimes\pi_{b,a}(t)s$. The same equality holds for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms and hence for the canonical comparisons in the localized category.

proof.text: For $c\geq b\geq a$, both normalization paths on the same K-flat models take $((u\otimes t)\otimes s)\otimes v$ to $u\otimes\pi_{c,a}(t)\pi_{b,a}(s)v$. Indeed the two-stage path gives $u\otimes\pi_{b,a}(\pi_{c,b}(t)s)v$, which is this expression because the quotient maps are ring homomorphisms and compose. The other path first identifies the last two extensions by the same balancing isomorphism and gives the same expression. Equality on these local tensor generators gives equality of sheaf maps, chain maps, and derived maps. For $b=a$, the formula is $(u\otimes t)\otimes s\mapsto u\otimes ts$, the unit identification. This proves the cocycle and unit identities using the explicit change-of-rings tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; K-flatness needed to compute the successive derived extensions is supplied by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings].
